pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' plus a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test checks the exact <li> text for high, normal and low items.
'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters, including id order.
'AC-4' test checks / lists all items in id order.
'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The code uses a Set check on searchParams.has.

The 'AC-7' test covers the no-match message for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' on an empty table in all four views. The spec's 'verified by review: checked by hand' step is empty, but the test proves the item. See the finding on the spec edit.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The checker change and the fake-app update let a query route pass.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' (af5f24d), edits acceptance item AC-7 after the go. It splices '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the item mid-sentence. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. 'checked by hand' is not a followable review step. The edit leaves AC-7 garbled, and the PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit, since the test already proves it. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision. Correct the PR's 'Changed after the go' line.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but af5f24d changes AC-7 after the go.
findings.fix: State the AC-7 edit in the PR, or revert it.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change follows its decisions: existing items get normal, and only high and low are labelled.
All 8 items have named tests and all 4 state rows are covered. The late AC-7 edit is a finding.
The tests assert exact rendered output and status codes, and would fail on wrong code. I did not run them here. CI is declared to run them.
README documents the filter. The labels are not mentioned, which is minor.
No defects found. The priority is bound as a parameter and validated against a Set, and the title is HTML-escaped.
The query value is allow-listed, SQL is parameterised, and no planted instructions were found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files, and I'm treating that as no UI to design-review.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate. The PR states no screenshots.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
